summary: Hybrid architecture: Go + Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL serving React + Vite (SPA), hosted on AWS ECS on Fargate (eu-central-1 Frankfurt). Estimated $500-1,800/month (around the $1,500 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: A modular API service for accounts, billing and persistence plus stateful realtime collaboration servers that scale independently for 5,000 concurrent connections. Over-engineering guard: microservices rejected: 5 engineer(s) cannot absorb the operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Web - React + Vite (SPA): Chosen because team already works in typescript (team.languages); React ecosystem has mature canvas (tldraw, Excalidraw) and Yjs CRDT bindings for collaborative editing; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=5; rich client-side interactivity for a realtime_collab.

alternatives.why_not: React + Vite scores higher on cost (fit 7.0 vs 7.1).
React + Vite scores higher on fit for the project type and cost (fit 6.6 vs 7.1).

tradeoffs: Routing/data fetching choices left to the team

backend.justification: Chosen because strong performance (5/5) with priorities.performance=5; strong scalability (5/5) with priorities.scalability=5; team already works in go (team.languages); lightweight concurrency for many persistent WebSocket connections.

alternatives.why_not: No csharp/fsharp in team.languages: ramp-up time and hiring risk. Go scores higher on realtime support and concurrency handling (fit 8.5 vs 9.9).
No elixir in team.languages: ramp-up time and hiring risk. Go scores higher on cost (fit 8.2 vs 9.9).

tradeoffs: Fewer batteries: more code for CRUD/admin
Verbose error handling slows feature work

database.choice: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL (eu-central-1 Frankfurt, HA standby)
database.justification: Chosen because relational integrity and transactions for a realtime_collab domain; strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=4; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=5. Managed as Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL: same platform and private network as the application hosting; managed failover/standby available.

alternatives.why_not: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 6.7 vs 7.7).
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 5.9 vs 7.7).
A close runner-up with a slightly weaker overall fit (fit 2.1 vs 2.3).
Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=managed_cloud: self-managed VMs/databases are excluded in favour of managed services.

tradeoffs: Single-writer primary: write scale beyond one large node needs partitioning/sharding
Vacuum and connection pooling need attention at scale

hosting.justification: Chosen because strong scalability (5/5) with priorities.scalability=5; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=5; autoscaling absorbs spiky traffic.

alternatives.why_not: AWS ECS on Fargate scores higher on scalability and traffic elasticity (fit 6.0 vs 6.5).
Only best-effort session affinity for stateful rooms (fit 5.9 vs 6.5).

tradeoffs: VPC, load balancer and NAT setup add fixed cost and complexity
